subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Human Error Is a System Problem
description: A 60-second lesson on Human Error Is a System Problem.

hook.text: A tired engineer types the wrong command and deletes a production database. Is it their fault—or the system's?

buildup.text: Investigations often blame the 'human error' of the last person who touched the system before failure.

discovery.text: Systems thinking says: if a human can easily make a catastrophic mistake, the system is poorly designed.

twist.text: Adding confirmation dialogs, safe defaults, and rollback capabilities prevents human errors from becoming disasters.

climax.text: Amazon's deployment system requires two people to approve production changes. The system catches what humans miss.

punchline.text: Don't blame the human. Fix the system that allowed it.

quiz.question: What does systems thinking say about human error?
options: A system that allows easy catastrophic mistakes is poorly designed
